raw_segments.text: 15. In the faith in what? In the love for what? In the hope of what? These weaklings!--they also, forsooth, wish to be the strong some time, there is no doubt about it, some time their kingdom also must come.

16. In the love for what? Make up by what? Dante, as it seems to me, made a crass mistake when with awe-inspiring ingenuity he placed that inscription over the gate of his hell. Me too made eternal love.

17. At any rate the following inscription would have a much better right to stand over the gate of the Christian Paradise, and its eternal blessedness. Me too made eternal hate, granted, of course, that a truth may rightly stand over the gate to a lie. For what is the blessedness of that Paradise? Possibly we could quickly surmise it, but it is better that it should be explicitly attested by an authority who in such matters is not to be disparaged, Thomas of Aquinas, the great Teacher and Saint.
18. Beati in regno celesti, says he, as gently as a lamb, vied bunt ponas damnatorum, ut beatituto elis magi's complaisat.

19. Or if we wish to hear a stronger tone, a word from the mouth of a triumphant Father of the Church, who warned his disciples against the cruel ecstasies of the public spectacles, but why? Faith offers us much more, says he, Despectac, c. 29ss.

30. Something much stronger. Thanks to the redemption, joys of quite another kind stand at our disposal. Instead of athletes we have our martyrs. We wish for blood, well, we have the blood of Christ but what then awaits us on the day of his return, of his triumph.
And then does he proceed, does this enraptured visionary?
21. Come, Ipso, Jove, Et, Ipsis, Swayze, Testibus, Inimis, Tenabris, Congemescence.
22. Item, Presides, the Provincial Governors, Persecutors, Deminicide, Naminees, Sivirubus, Quam, Ipsis, Flamis, Sivirunt, Insultant, Tibis, Contra, Christianos, Lquecents.
23. Quos, Pridaria, Sapiens, Elos, Philosophos, Coram, Disipulis, Swayze, Unicon, Flagrant, Tibis, Erubus, Sinc.
Tunk Magi's Trajodia Dindi, Magi's Silicet Vocals, With Louder Tones and More Violent
Shrieks, Insua Propria Calamitate, Tunk Histrion's Cognicendi, Soluteer's Molto per Ignum, Tunk
Spectandus Auriga Inflamia Rhodotodus Rubens, Tunk Zeistesai Contemplandi Non Engymnosas,
Said in Enjaculati, Nysai quod Nietunk Quitum Elos Velum Vivos, Utquimallum ad Eius Podius
Conspectum Insatiableum Confera, Quiendominum Severunt, Hicastole, Dickum Fabri out Quistuari
Philius, As is shown by the whole of the following, and in particular by this well-known description
of the mother of Jesus from the Talmud, Tertullian is henceforth referring to the Jews.
Sabadi destructor, Samarites et demonium habens, Hicast quemajuderidimistes,
Hicast ole erindinet calaphis diverberatus, sputimentis de decoratus, fel et acid potatus.
Hicast, quem clam descent subrepurant, Utresorexis dicature vel horchalanus detracts it,
Ne lacticis sui frequentia commentium lateranter, Ut talia species, Ut talibus exalts,
Quiestibai praetor out consul out sacerdos de sua liberallitate prastibit,
Et tamen hic jam habemus quadimodo per phytum spiritu imaginante representata,
Sedarum qualia alasunt, Quienech oculus viditnech oris audivitnech in core hominis ascenderunt.
Eichor Roman II, IX, Credo circo et atracavia, first and fourth row,
or, according to others, the comic and the tragic stay, et omni studio gradira, per phytum,
so stands it written.

raw_segments.text: 15. In the faith in what? In the love for what? In the hope of what? These weaklings,
they also forsooth wish to be the strong sometime. There is no doubt about it. Sometime their
kingdom also must come. The kingdom of God is their name for it, as has been mentioned.
They are so meek in everything. Yet in order to experience that kingdom it is necessary
to live long, to live beyond death, yes. Eternal life is necessary so that one can make up
forever for that earthly life in faith. In love. In hope.

what is the blessedness of that Paradise? Possibly we could quickly surmise it, but it
is better that it should be explicitly attested by an authority who in such matters is not

church, who warned his disciples against the cruel ecstasies of the public spectacles,

banter, cum ipso jove et ipsis sways testibus inimis tenebris congemisense. Item presides,
the provincial governors, persecutors diminisae niminis siviribus, quam ipsi flammis sivirunt
insultentibus contra Cristiano's liquescence. Quos prederia sapiens, illos philosophos quorum,
dissipulis sways una conflagrantibus irubescence, quibis nile ad diem pertner suaidibent, quibis
animas out nullas out non in pristine corpora redituras affirmabent. Eschium poetas non ad
radamantinac ad minwa, said ad inapanati Christi tribunal palpitants. Tunk magi's
traggio dea diendi, magi's silicet vocals, with louder tones and more violent shrieks,

nysae quod nietunk quitum illos vellum vivos, utquimallum ad eus podius conspectum insatiableum

ut resorexis dicature vell horchalanus detracts it, nylactiki sui frequentia commientium
lateranter. Ut talia species, ut talibus exalts, quiese tibi praetor out consul out
sacerdos de sua liberallitate prastabit. Et taman hic jam habemus quadimodo perphytum
spiritu imaginante reprisantata. Ceterum qualia a la sunt, quinec oculus viditnec oris
odavitnec in core hominis ascenderunt. I core Roman II, IX, Credo Serco et atracavia,
first and fourth row, or, according to others, the comic and the tragic stay, et omni studio
gratura. Perphytum, so stands it written.
